messages:
maria: heads up — I just saw SavedSearches from Org B show up in Org A's console after I did a super-fast org switch a few times. repro steps below.

maria: steps: quick-switch from A -> B -> A using the top-left picker, open Insights -> Saved Searches. sometimes you get B's entries for ~2s then it snaps back.

maria: attaching the minimal proxy log I collected (snip):
```
[proxy] recv req id=abc123 headers: x-org-id=A x-auth=ey... route=console/prefetch
[proxy] fallback to prefetch handler id=abc123 cache_hit=false
[proxy] prefetch: stash key=console:prefetch:org=A -> downstream call to /internal/prefetch?target=insights
[proxy] downstream responded 200 payload=[...]
[proxy] observed downstream response had X-Owner-Org=B (?!)
[proxy] served UI payload to user org=A (with B rows)
```

maria: I think there's a race where prefetch/downstream picks up a stale tenant header when the router falls back to the legacy matcher.

ashok: ugh. sounds like header normalization race. did you get the auth token used in that call? any chance of impersonation?

maria: token in logs is the user's session token for org A. I dumped the internal call trace — the internal prefetch call to /internal/insights had headers: x-source-org=A but the response had rows tagged with org B id (server-side).

dan: can you grep recent rollout changes? last week we flipped the router-affinity patch that changes header forwarding when route-matcher returns 404 -> fallback. maybe that path doesn't scrub the old route metadata.

maria: checking. router-affinity PR #4123 merged Tue night. I reproduced on staging after that merge.

lia: is this tied to the caching layer? quick switch triggers a prefetch with cache key maybe not including the new org id if the header isn't applied atomically.

maria: yep, prefetch cache key is computed in the gateway before the fallback happens. if fallback path obtains the wrong tenant tag later, cached payload can be returned with mismatched org rows.

ashok: short mitigation: force gateway to include explicit org-id in cache key and scrub any owner headers from downstream responses. We should also stop forwarding any X-Org-Hint from internal services to client payloads.

dan: I can push a small gating change to the router: when matcher returns fallback, compute cache key using request's canonical org header (not the matcher-derived field). Quick canary to staging first.

maria: +1. also want telemetry: emit a metric when returned payload org id != request org id so we can quantify blast radius. might be useful for retrospective.

lia: I'll add an eval to console e2e to hammer quick-switch for 60s and assert no foreign rows present.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by dan for branch router-scrub-orgkey to staging at commit f1a2b3.

maria: assigning owners: dan for router fix + canary, ashok for cache-key change, lia for e2e, i'll own rollback + incident doc.

ashok: for Dedicated customers we should also check the prefetch worker pool — it pulls tenant context from a worker-local cache. I'll audit that code.

lia: created a short dashboard: "org-mismatch-prefetch" showing metric counts and top offending services. sending to #eng-sre.

sre-bot: alert: org-mismatch-prefetch > 0 on staging — 12 occurrences in last 10m.

dan: rolled to staging canary. early telemetry: 0 mismatches for first 5m. lia running e2e now.

maria: lia reports one repro in canary during a race. looks like cache-key change is required too. ashok can you open patch for cache key and scrubbing?

ashok: will open PR today and target staging. also adding unit tests for cache-key composition and a lint rule preventing forwarding X-Owner-* headers in proxy responses.

maria: thanks. follow-up plan: 1) patch router+cache 2) run 30m canary with e2e 3) monitor telemetry 4) promote to prod if zero mismatches for 30m. I'll draft incident note after prod rollout.

lia: notes: UX PM asked if we should slow down quick-switch debounce to reduce the race surface — making a UX ticket now.

maria: FYI security review requested because this is a cross-tenant exposure. marking for triage and legal review if any customer data left the org boundary.

dan: thumbsup. I'll post the canary link and logs in this thread once done.

maria: thanks everyone :heart:
